All-Stars Host Ken Jennings Announcer Johnny Gilbert Broadcast ABC: March 13, 2026 – May 15, 2026 Packager Sony Pictures Television Studios Celebrity Jeopardy! is a spinoff that features celebrities competing in the classic quiz show to win money for their favorite charities. It started out as a series of special weeks on the regular show, and later it was spoofed in a series of Saturday Night Live (SNL) shorts; now the show is its own primetime series. Contents 1 Gameplay 1.1 Money Amounts 1.2 Tournament Structure 1.3 Winnings 2 Contestants 3 Game Summary 4 Trivia 5 See Also 6 References Gameplay[] Money Amounts[] Rounds Amounts Total Jeopardy! $100-$500 $9,000 Double Jeopardy! $200-$1,000 $18,000 Triple Jeopardy! $300-$1,500 $27,000 NOTE: The celebrities' charities, don't actually get the money scored in each match. For as with all tournaments, the scores are kept in points (dollar signs are kept for aesthetic purposes). So, as you look at the summary below, ignore the dollar signs and pretend that they are really point values. Tournament Structure[] The Tournament Structure is basically the same as the one in the 1990 Super Jeopardy! tournament, the 1993 Jeopardy! 10th Anniversary Tournament, the 1996 Jeopardy! Olympic Games Tournament, the Jeopardy! International Tournament, 2005 Jeopardy! Ultimate Tournament of Champions, the 2014 Jeopardy! Battle of the Decades tournament preliminary round, the 2022 Jeopardy! National College Championship, the Jeopardy! Second Chance tournament, the 2023 Jeopardy! High School Reunion Tournament, the 2023 Jeopardy! Champions Wildcard tournament, the 2024 Champions Wildcard tournament, the Jeopardy! Tournament of Champions since 2022, the Jeopardy! Invitational Tournament in 2024 and 2025, and the Pop Culture Jeopardy! tournament: No wild cards, it's "win or go home". Just like the Jeopardy! Tournament of Champions in 2022, 2025 and 2026, six quarterfinal games is played. The winner of each game will advance to the semifinals with the three seeded Celebrity champions where the three winners from those games will compete in the final for $1,000,000 to their favorite charity. Kamau Bell # SF #3 May 14, 2026 Ike Barinholtz # Final May 15, 2026 # Trivia[] This tournament brought back 21 players from the 2022–2023 Celebrity Jeopardy!, 2023–2024 Celebrity Jeopardy!, and 2025 Celebrity Jeopardy! tournaments.[2] This is the second Celebrity Jeopardy! event to bring back all players who have previously appeared on Celebrity Jeopardy! events, the first being the 2009–2010 Jeopardy! Million Dollar Celebrity Invitational tournament. This tournament was set to air on February 27, 2025, but it was postponed to two weeks later. Out of all three primetime Celebrity Jeopardy! tournament finals, the only tournament to bring back all three players from the finals was the 2023–2024 Celebrity Jeopardy! tournament, which featured Lisa Ann Walter, Mo Rocca, and Katie Nolan. This is the fourth tournament where all three players from the finals in a different tournament were brought back to compete. The other ones were the 2022 Jeopardy! Tournament of Champions, the 2025 Jeopardy! Champions Wildcard and the 2025 Jeopardy! Tournament of Champions. Unlike the Jeopardy! Tournament of Champions in 2022, 2025, and 2026, an exhibition match will not be held between Ike Barinholtz, Lisa Ann Walter, and W. Kamau Bell, who received a bye to the semifinals. Mo Rocca, Andy Richter, and Steven Weber are the only three contestants who have played on Celebrity Jeopardy! in the Trebek era before the primetime tournaments. Mo Rocca previously appeared in the 2015 Celebrity Jeopardy! event, losing to John Berman. Andy Richter previously appeared in the 1999 Celebrity Jeopardy! event, defeating Brian Dennehy and Sharon Epatha Merkerson, and the 2009–2010 Jeopardy! Million Dollar Celebrity Invitational tournament, defeating Wolf Blitzer and Dana Delany in the quarterfinals. Due to a scheduling conflict losing The Tonight Show with Conan O'Brien, Andy dropped out of the 2009–2010 Jeopardy! Million Dollar Celebrity Invitational tournament semifinals. His spot was replaced by Isaac Mizrahi. Steven Weber previously appeared in the Trebek-era inaugural Celebrity Jeopardy! event, losing to Cheech Marin. See Also[] Jeopardy! Super Jeopardy! Jep!
